description.narrative: TradeMark Africa's Quality and Value of Traded Goods Portfolio works to remove standards and sanitary and phytosanitary compliance as a barrier to African exports, recognising that the ability to consistently meet international market requirements is the gateway to accessing higher-value regional and global trade opportunities, particularly as global buyers apply increasingly stringent environmental, social, and governance standards to production and supply chains. The Portfolio supports national standards bureaux to strengthen laboratory capacity, inspection and certification services, and conformity assessment infrastructure; works with governments to implement technical regulations consistent with WTO trade rules; facilitates harmonisation of standards frameworks at national, regional, and continental levels; pursues Mutual Recognition Agreements to build cross-border confidence in conformity assessment; and supports enterprises directly, with a focus on agricultural value chains and SMEs, to raise their compliance levels, access certification services, and connect to export markets. Across these interventions, the Portfolio's approach is to build durable national and regional quality infrastructure that enables African producers to trade on the basis of a single assessment, reducing duplication, lowering costs, and improving the predictability of cross-border trade.

recipient-country.narrative: TradeMark Africa (TMA) accelerates economic integration across 20 sub-Saharan nations by designing regional programmes that reduce trade barriers, lower transit costs, and digitize border infrastructure. Spanning East, West, Central, Southern Africa, and the Horn, these initiatives modernise critical maritime ports and key trade corridors by replacing paper-heavy customs processes with automated digital single-window systems. By targeting green trade corridor development, supporting women and small businesses in cross-border trade, and mobilizing private capital through its commercial arm, Trade Catalyst Africa, TMA directly facilitates trade flow alignment with the African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA) frameworks.

receiver-org.narrative: TradeMark Africa (TMA) is a leading Aid-for-Trade organisation founded in 2010 to grow intra-African trade, increase Africa’s share in global trade, and make trade more pro-poor and sustainable. We operate on a not-for-profit basis, funded by a strong coalition of development partners including Canada, Denmark, the European Union, Finland, France, the Gates Foundation, Ireland, the Mastercard Foundation, the Netherlands, Norway, Sweden and the United Kingdom. TMA works closely with regional and continental institutions, national governments, the private sector, and civil society to unlock trade and investment opportunities across the continent.

We operate on a not-for-profit basis, funded by a strong coalition of development partners including Canada, Denmark, the European Union, Finland, France, the Gates Foundation, Ireland, the Mastercard Foundation, the Netherlands, Norway, Sweden and the United Kingdom. TMA works closely with regional and continental institutions, national governments, the private sector, and civil society to unlock trade and investment opportunities across the continent.
